content.text:
For a **typical cold**, there’s no medicine that “cures” it—most improve on their own in about **7–10 days**. Treatment is mainly for **symptom relief**, and antibiotics usually don’t help because colds are viral. ([cdc.gov](https://www.cdc.gov/common-cold/treatment/index.html?utm_source=openai))

**Common options for adults:**

- **Fever, headache, sore throat, body aches:**  
  **Acetaminophen** or **ibuprofen**. Avoid taking more than the label dose, and don’t combine multiple products that contain acetaminophen.

- **Stuffy nose/sinus congestion:**  
  **Saline nasal spray/rinse** is safest. A decongestant like **pseudoephedrine** may help, but ask a pharmacist/doctor first if you have **high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, prostate/urination problems**, or take certain medications.

- **Runny nose/sneezing:**  
  An antihistamine may help, but some cause drowsiness.

- **Cough:**  
  **Honey** can help cough in adults and children over 1 year old. Some people use **dextromethorphan** for dry cough or **guaifenesin** for mucus, though benefits vary. ([cdc.gov](https://www.cdc.gov/acute-bronchitis/about/index.html?utm_source=openai))

- **General care:**  
  Rest, fluids, humidified air/steam, and throat lozenges can help.

**Avoid/important cautions:**
- Don’t use **antibiotics** unless a clinician says you have a bacterial infection.
- Be careful with “multi-symptom” cold medicines—they can duplicate ingredients.
- For **children**, especially under 4–6 years, don’t give OTC cough/cold medicines unless a clinician recommends it; they can cause serious side effects. ([fda.gov](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/understanding-over-counter-medicines/frequently-asked-question-childrens-cough-and-cold-medicines?utm_source=openai))

**Seek medical advice urgently** if you have trouble breathing, chest pain, severe/worsening symptoms, fever that’s high or lasts more than a few days, symptoms lasting >10 days without improvement, dehydration, or if you’re high-risk. Also consider testing for **COVID-19 or flu**, because antivirals may help if started early for those illnesses. ([cdc.gov](https://www.cdc.gov/common-cold/treatment/index.html?utm_source=openai))
